\title{Correctness-Gated Policy Optimization for Streaming-Accelerator RTL:
A Failure-Aware Post-Route Study}

\author{Mohamed Amine Hallam%
\thanks{Mohamed Amine Hallam is with Harbin Institute of Technology,
Shenzhen, China (e-mail: hallamamine05@gmail.com).}%
% Add the supervisor and any other qualifying co-authors here only after every
% author has reviewed and approved the complete submission.
}

\maketitle

\begin{abstract}
Improving the best generated register-transfer-level (RTL) implementation does
not establish that a generator produces useful hardware more reliably.  We
study correctness-gated policy optimization for streaming accelerators using
an endpoint that preserves sample multiplicity and assigns zero frequency to
incorrect or implementation-failed draws.  An executable oracle gates a learned
physical reward during training; Vivado post-route implementation supplies the
evaluation evidence.  On a separately frozen
\studyclaim{StudyTwoDesignCount}-design split, two policy-training seeds sharing
one supervised fine-tuned (SFT) checkpoint and a canonicalization-aware
random-forest (RF) reward raise failure-penalized timing-derived maximum
frequency from
\studyclaim{StudyTwoOverallSftPenalized} to
\studyclaim{StudyTwoOverallRfPenalized}~MHz.  The paired gain is
\studyclaim{StudyTwoOverallRfSftGain}~MHz, with a
\studyclaim{StudyTwoBootstrapConfidence}\% design-bootstrap interval of
[\studyclaim{StudyTwoOverallRfSftCiLow},
\studyclaim{StudyTwoOverallRfSftCiHigh}]~MHz.  Both RF seeds improve; a
single-seed correctness-only control improves functional yield but lowers the
physical endpoint.  RF also exceeds the original multilayer-perceptron reward
package, without isolating model class from representation changes.  The gain
comes with more LUTs and registers, fewer DSP blocks, slightly higher vectorless
power, and a small matched VerilogEval regression.  Post-primary setup-closure
and board checks support the physical direction on descriptive subsets, while
median-filter results remain weak.  These findings support a bounded
distribution-level improvement within the studied accelerator generators, not
general RTL superiority or a universal power--performance--area gain.
\end{abstract}

\begin{IEEEkeywords}
FPGA physical design, hardware-aware optimization, large language models,
reinforcement learning, reward-model reliability, RTL generation
\end{IEEEkeywords}
